items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: I hear Charlie Parker and I stop and say oh wow, check that out what he did going through that chord change.

ctx.x: a lot of jazz musicians in terms of the academic community would always say oh those jazz musicians play out of tune. Because they don’t recognize it’s coming from a different source. And it’s not going to have that kind of thing because it’s not that type of music in its purest form. So you can’t use that as a barometer to negate or whatever. It’s all music, but all musics have their particular parameters that codify what that music is. So in understanding — and there’s also the argument in the African-American…

mission and I have no problem with him, that’s what he does, it’s music that you can talk over, have in the background. It’s not like when I hear Charlie Parker and I stop and say oh wow, check that out what he did going through that chord change. You know Kenny’s found his niche and hey, God bless him. He’s doing his thing. But it’s just very interesting when people in situations like this take it upon themselves to make these wild assumptions and to misinform people. And we need to do away with that kind of…
